linked.job: Wipes drives completely, with proof it was done.
linked.name: Beerus — Destruct Key Pro
linked.note: Beerus's other form: a bootable USB stick of its own — a drive is wiped by booting from the stick, for machines that are off or being decommissioned whole. The Beerus app in this bundle runs the same engine on a machine that is already running. Get the image from the Beerus repo.

notes: Flat layout: every tool's files sit together in this one folder — the bundle adds no per-tool folders of its own. A tool keeps only the structure its own portable edition ships with (Charon's Charon folder and NitroCore's _internal folder are part of those tools). The one exception is Beerus's folder, which exists to answer the _internal collision described below.

One file-name collision, resolved openly: all five portable editions carry a file named README-PORTABLE.txt, each with different contents. In this bundle each is kept as README-PORTABLE-<Tool>.txt — contents unchanged; only the name is qualified, so nothing overwrites anything.

A second collision, resolved openly: Beerus Portable and NitroCore are both one-folder apps whose support folder is named _internal, and both zips put that folder at the top level — two different support folders cannot share one name in one folder. So Beerus sits in a Beerus folder inside this bundle (the same shape Charon ships in): Beerus.exe and its _internal, byte for byte as released; only where they sit is different. Its start file is Beerus/Beerus.exe.

Argus portable mode: starting Argus from the launcher (or from Argus-Portable.bat) keeps its settings, scan history, and quarantine vault in the ArgusData folder inside this folder, so they travel with the bundle.

Beerus Portable keeps its work records beside its own start file: certificates of destruction land in Beerus/certificates, and its file, folder, and free-space wipe reports in Beerus/certificates/reports. They are the technician's job records; they travel with this folder.
